comparison.measured_cost: The concept increases the header from 160px to 241px at 1440x900, 158px to 239px at 390x844, 145px to 221px at 844x390, and 158px to 239px at 320x568.
comparison.strength: Shortest implementation and direct native keyboard/touch operation.
comparison.loss: A permanent utility field takes 76-81px from the map-facing header at every neutral visit and makes the atlas read more like a dashboard.

comparison.direction: explicit Places action and existing panel
comparison.live_host: Existing map-header action row plus existing panel dock
comparison.new_state: One ephemeral placesOpen boolean and one trigger ref; no URL/state-machine expansion.
comparison.measured_cost: The neutral shell gains one 44px action; the existing 400px desktop dock or current mobile sheet appears only after activation. The matched prototype keeps zero horizontal overflow at all four measured sizes.
comparison.strength: Lowest default visual footprint, truthful Places title, deliberate focus entry, and reuse of the mature panel shell.
comparison.loss: More state/focus wiring than an inline select; the open compact sheet temporarily covers map controls, as existing expanded panels do.
Leaves the named-place retrieval problem unsolved, especially where labels overlap or a reader knows a name but not its map position.

comparison.new_state: Would require broadening panelOpen and repairing title/focus/history side effects.
comparison.measured_cost: Would reserve 400px on desktop or mount a bottom sheet before the reader asks for it.
comparison.strength: None over the explicit panel once reachability is considered.
comparison.loss: Unreachable as proposed and misleading if made permanent.

ponytail_ruling: Choose the explicit Places action/panel. It is not the fewest lines, but it is the smallest product footprint that solves the actual retrieval problem. Reuse native select, the loaded Geo array, handleSelect, ExplorerPanelNav, and the existing dock; add no component library, custom combobox, search, router, panel stack, or camera behavior.
